title: How We Work: Communication Rhythms & Decision Rights
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This document records Redwood’s opinionated approach to communication, meeting cadence, and decision-making. It is intended for all employees and managers as a single source of truth when setting up team rhythms and onboarding new hires.

Scope
- Applies to product, engineering, research, go-to-market, and core functions unless a team-level policy explicitly replaces a section below.

Key Principles
- Default to async: prioritize written updates and Confluence for decisions unless live discussion is required.
- Clear owners: every project, doc, and recurring meeting must have a named owner and a fallback.
- Time-boxed synchronous work: keep most meetings to 30 minutes or less; use focused agendas.
- Document decisions: capture outcomes, options considered, and rollout impact in a Decision Record (link to related template).

Communication Rhythms

Company-level
1. All-Hands (Company): weekly, 45 minutes. Leadership updates, product demos, and two Q&A slots. Owner: CEO.
2. Product Showcase: bi-weekly, 60 minutes. Cross-functional demos; opt-in by product teams. Owner: Head of Product.
3. Town Halls (Quarterly): 90 minutes. Strategy deep-dive + AMAs. Owner: Executive Staff.

Team-level (recommended defaults)
- Weekly Team Sync: 30 minutes. Tactical status, blockers, and action item review. Owner: Team lead.
- Bi-weekly Planning: 90 minutes (PM + Eng + SRE). Roadmap and capacity alignment.
- Monthly OKR Review: 60 minutes. Progress vs key results and risk register.
- Office Hours: 1 hour/week by rotation for cross-team questions and unblockers.

Async conventions
- Use Confluence for all decision drafts and major specs. Template: "Problem / Options / Recommendation / Rollout / Metrics".
- Use Slack threads for short-lived discussions. Prefer a summary back to Confluence when the outcome matters.
- Use PR descriptions that include a short “Why” and a link to the design doc; reviewers should add a one-line decision comment on merge.

Meeting Best Practices
- Publish agenda 24 hours before meetings; add time-boxed items.
- Appoint a facilitator, note-taker, and a decisions recorder for each session.
- Circulate notes and action items within 24 hours.
- If a meeting grows beyond scope, convert to a focused working session with a pre-read and explicit goals.

Decision Rights Framework

Overview
- Redwood uses a 3-level decision model to reduce bottlenecks and clarify accountability. Each decision must be annotated with its level and recorded on Confluence.

Decision levels (table)
- Level 1 — Delegated (Team): everyday implementation choices that do not change cross-team contracts or infra. Owner: Team Lead / Feature Owner. Examples: API parameter renames that are backwards compatible, UX copy tweaks.
- Level 2 — Cross-team (Functional Impact): changes that affect multiple teams or service contracts; requires consultation with impacted teams. Owner: Product Area Lead or Engineering Manager. Examples: schema changes that need migration, significant latency vs cost tradeoffs.
- Level 3 — Strategic (Company-wide): changes to core infra, pricing, or compliance posture; requires Exec approval and a documented rollout. Owner: Executive Sponsor. Examples: adopting a new hosting region, changes to SLAs offered to customers.

Decision process checklist
1. Draft: write a short Confluence decision record using the template.
2. Review: gather input from reviewers identified in the template (minimum: owner, two cross-team reviewers for Level 2, exec sponsor for Level 3).
3. Approve: owner publishes the decision and assigns rollout steps.
4. Communicate: broadcast to affected teams via Slack #announcements and update relevant runbooks.
5. Monitor: attach success metrics and a 30/90-day review item.

RACI guidance (example)
- Responsible: feature owner or service owner.
- Accountable: team lead or area lead.
- Consulted: cross-functional SMEs (SRE, Security, Product).
- Informed: downstream dependents and support teams.

Onboarding & Role Expectations (how rhythms plug in)

New hire 30/60/90 (high level)
- Day 0–7: orientation, security access, first team sync attendance, buddy assignment, complete core trainings.
- Week 2–4: own a small task, present a 1-page runbook/update at team sync, schedule a manager check-in.
- Month 2–3: own a cross-functional ticket, contribute to an OKR review, prepare feedback for performance calibration.

Role & career ladder touchpoints
- Managers should review the relevant role rubric during week 2 and schedule a career conversation by week 4.
- ICs are expected to demonstrate ownership (Level 1 decisions), document designs, and mentor peers.
- People-ops will auto-schedule a career growth touchpoint at 3 months for all new hires.

Benefits & Working Flexibilities (high level)
- Flexible PTO policy: take time off as needed while ensuring coverage with your team.
- Hybrid work guidance: core collaboration days are team-defined; default policy is 3 collaboration days/week unless role-specific needs apply.
- Office stipend & ergonomic program: provisioning process is via the internal procurement portal (link).
- Care time & parental support: short-term caregiver leave and phased return plans are available via People Ops.

Internal tools and access patterns

Tools (primary)
- Slack: daily communications and incident channels. Naming: #team-<name>, #proj-<shortcode>, #inc-<service>.
- Confluence: specs, decision records, onboarding pages. All major decisions must include a Confluence link in the PR description.
- GitHub: code, PRs, and issue tracking. Use labels: triage, needs-review, blocked, release.
- Okta / SSO: primary access management; group membership determines role-based access to infra.
- Internal Portal: single source for onboarding checklist, hardware requests, and stipend submissions.

Access provisioning checklist for managers
1. Submit new hire request in the Internal Portal.
2. Assign role-based Okta groups (Engineering-IC, Product-PM, Contractor-Limited).
3. Provision GitHub team membership and repository access.
4. Request cloud console access for infra owners (SRE approval required).
5. Confirm contributor has the onboarding checklist completed and schedule the 1-week check-in.

Deprovisioning (high level)
- Follow the standard offboarding checklist: revoke Okta sessions, remove repo access, reclaim hardware, and archive active Confluence drafts. Aim to complete within 48 hours of exit confirmation.

Conflict & Escalation Guidelines
- For disagreements at Level 1: escalate to the team lead for a decision within 3 business days.
- For Level 2 disagreements: convene an impact review with the area lead and at least one cross-team reviewer; timeline: 7 business days.
- For Level 3 conflicts: executive sponsor mediation with a documented final decision; timeline: depends on customer or compliance urgency.

Metrics & Continuous Improvement
- People Ops will review adoption metrics quarterly: percent of decisions recorded, average time-to-decision by level, and meeting load per role.
- Teams are encouraged to run a 90-day experiment for any change in rhythm (e.g., swapping weekly team sync to a bi-weekly async report) and report results.

- Review cadence: annually or after any company-level organizational change.

Appendix: Quick Templates

Confluence decision record (minimal)
- Title: short descriptive name
- Owner: name + team
- Decision level: 1 | 2 | 3
- Problem statement: 2–4 lines
- Options considered: 1–3 bullets
- Recommendation: single sentence
- Rollout plan & rollback steps: bullets with owners
- Success metrics: 1–3 metrics and review dates

Meeting agenda template
1. Objective (1 sentence)
2. Timeboxed items (3–5 lines with owners and timers)
3. Decisions needed (explicit asks)
4. Parking lot / next steps
